chunks: A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Khalid, from Abu Ismail, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Can a man pray upon Abu Qubays facing the Qiblah?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no objection.'

key_terms.أَبُو قُبَيْسٍ: Abu Qubays (a mountain near the Kaaba in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray on top of Mount Abu Qubays facing the Qiblah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of praying atop Mount Abu Qubays, a prominent landmark adjacent to the Kaaba, by affirming that facing the Qiblah there is valid. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the principle that the sanctity of the Kaaba extends to its immediate vicinity, allowing for flexible prayer locations as long as the directional orientation is maintained. It serves as a practical legal precedent for worshippers in Mecca regarding the validity of Salah in elevated or specific topographical spots near the Holy Sanctuary.

en.hubeali: A group, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed from Fazalat, from Al Husayn Bin Usman, from Ibn Muskan, from Khalid, from Abu Ismail who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Can the man pray Salāt upon (Mount) Abu Qubays facing the Qiblah?’ So heasws said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 19. A group has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthman from ibn Muskan from Khalid abu ’Isma‘il who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Can one perform Salah (prayer) on abu Qubays (name of the hill) facing the direction of al-Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah)? He (the Imam) said, ‘There is no offense in it.”’
